title: ledger TSV with CRLF line endings + a valid row -> the row still parses -> VERIFIED
spec_case: V6: ledger TSV with CRLF line endings + a valid row. Expected: row still parses -> VERIFIED (explicit CRLF-handling verdict).
path_convention: substitute @FIXTURE_ROOT@ with the ROOT printed by make-fixture.sh (FIXTURE_READY V6 <ROOT>); make-fixture.sh also writes the substituted copy to <ROOT>/expected.json. probes[].ledger and probes[].target are relative to the fixture root.
ledger_header: source_path	source_sha256	vault_path	vault_sha256	exported_at	note
live_ledger_untouched: corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv stays header-only; the builder never writes it (test ledgers live under tests/vault/ and the fixture root)

crlf_contract.line_endings: CRLF on every line (header and row): exactly 2 CR bytes, 2 lines, each line ending CR LF
crlf_contract.what_must_hold: the CRLF ledger parses exactly like the LF control: the valid row still matches -> VERIFIED(moved-to-obsidian)
crlf_contract.lf_control: @FIXTURE_ROOT@/ledger-lf-control.tsv (identical row, LF endings; isolates CRLF as the only variable)
crlf_contract.truncated_boundary: @FIXTURE_ROOT@/ledger-crlf-truncated.tsv (CRLF row truncated after the 4 hash columns; the CR then rides on vault_sha256, so the digest comparison fails -> NOT-VERIFIED with a sha-mismatch reason). Informational boundary, NOT a judged probe: a schema-tolerant harness that strips CR from every field may legitimately still verify it, so no verdict is required of candidate harnesses here. selftest.sh pins it against the r2 tool.

probes.role: the assignment's case: CRLF header + CRLF valid row -> the row still parses -> VERIFIED
control: the identical row with LF endings; isolates CRLF as the only variable

targets.why: byte-identical source/vault pair plus a fully matching ledger row whose lines end CRLF; the trailing CR rides on the last column (note), so every hash column stays clean

accept.note: a harness may render the verdict as one token or as separate fields; both satisfy this case as long as the verdict class is VERIFIED (never NOT-VERIFIED) and the output names the moved-to-obsidian receipt that justified it

disarmed.method: point the tool at a header-only ledger: printf 'source_path\tsource_sha256\tvault_path\tvault_sha256\texported_at\tnote\n' > /tmp/empty.tsv; SOUJI_LEDGER=/tmp/empty.tsv tools/souji-verify.sh @FIXTURE_ROOT@/src/payload.md
disarmed.why: the row is the receipt: without it the byte-identical vault copy is not evidence

crosscheck_round2.note: the r2 tool tools/souji-verify.sh predates the r4 VERIFIED vocabulary; for these inputs its expected output is the same verdict pair under r2 names (measured; selftest.sh pins it)
crosscheck_round2.expected_line: VERDICT	@FIXTURE_ROOT@/src/payload.md	SAFE	moved-to-obsidian	ledger-row vault=@FIXTURE_ROOT@/vault/payload.md source-sha256=127ac886a92b
crosscheck_round2.seam: SOUJI_LEDGER env override (defaults to corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv, which stays header-only)

failure_modes_caught: CRLF-hostile ledger parsing: exact-equality header checks, $-anchored row matching, or any parser that treats the trailing CR as data in a way that rejects the row -> V6a flips from VERIFIED to NOT-VERIFIED

false VERIFIED on a mismatched pair: the sha columns must still decide; the fixture's hashes are the true digests, so a harness that skips the vault-side hash check cannot be caught here (V2/V4 own that) but a harness that skips CRLF handling is caught by V6a
always-NOT-VERIFIED stub: V6b (LF control) and V6a both require VERIFIED, so a harness that never verifies fails

consumers.runner-26: reads probes[] (per-probe ledger/target/verdict/contains); load-tested against this fixture (2 rows emitted)
consumers.runner-28: reads probes[] (per-probe ledger against the case dir, target against its --out root); full matrix run passed both V6 probes for impl-20 and impl-24
consumers.runner-29: explicit case-V6 probes branch: resolves probes[].ledger/target against its --out root with a case-dir fallback, and additionally judges ledger-crlf-truncated.tsv as NOT-VERIFIED(mismatch) when present — note that a CR-stripping candidate (impl-24) legitimately verifies the truncated row, so that extra row is stricter than this case's judged contract

determinism.note: fixed payload bytes and exported_at; ledger rows embed per-root absolute paths, so ledger file hashes vary per build root while the payload sha256 is constant

notes: The builder writes ONLY: <FIXTURE_ROOT>/** and <LEDGER> (default tests/vault/ledger-V6.tsv). The live ledger and the real vault /home/vgpnk/Documents/shokoknowledge are never read or written by this fixture; the vault-side copies live under the fixture root.
No Obsidian process, no CLI and no network are involved; the GUI launcher /usr/bin/obsidian is never executed.
stdout contract: line 1 = JSON {case,root,targets,expect,ledger,sha256}; line 2 = FIXTURE_READY V6 <ROOT>; --quiet emits FIXTURE_READY + KEY=VALUE lines only.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 build/assertion failure, 2 usage.
